stemMd: Aquaporins increase the speed of water movement across a membrane. Which statement remains true?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They force water to enter regardless of conditions.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The net direction depends on the water-potential difference.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They make the membrane freely permeable to proteins.

options.label: E
options.textMd: They pump water uphill using ATP directly.

explanationMd: Aquaporins increase water permeability but do not supply energy or determine a fixed direction. Water still moves down its water-potential gradient; the channel changes rate rather than the thermodynamic direction.

distractorRationale.e: Aquaporins are channels, not ATP-driven water pumps.
distractorRationale.a: Direction is not fixed by the channel.
distractorRationale.d: Water selectivity does not imply protein permeability.
distractorRationale.b: Channels function within an intact bilayer.
